checks.correction: LSJ does not gloss the adverb. It gives only 'Adv. -κῶς ib. QConv. 643c, Theo Sm. p.116 H.', so Plutarch comes first and 'numerically' is the gloss in Bailly and Sophocles. It is also untrue that the neuter is 'attested only as an Egyptian land tax'. Only LSJ's substantive sense III (τὸ -κόν) is the tax. LSJ II has the neuter predicative adjective 'τὸ ἓν ἁπλῶς οὐκ ἦν ἀ.' (Dam. Pr. 117). DGE has 'subst. τὸ ἀ. número cardinal' (D.T. 636.15, 637.25; Sch.D.T. 243.1). The scholia also use neuter ἀριθμητικόν ἐστι (Sch. Od. 9.246; Sch. Isocr.). The bearing 'the neuter adjective has no relevant sense' is therefore overstated.
